endorsements.quote: Systems assess and communicate ambiguity to call for human supervision when needed

As technological advances continue, clinicians will increasingly need to supervise AI outputs, interpret uncertainty, and decide when to override system recommendations (see the Levels of Autonomy and Risk section).

unlisted_practices: Shift AI benchmarking in mental health from static knowledge tests to dynamic evaluations of therapeutic capabilities.
Subject stand-alone autonomous therapy AI to very strong guardrails and extensive safety testing, as with any medical product.
Establish ethical standards, data-protection safeguards, regulatory and legal frameworks, and consumer information and protection provisions before deploying autonomous therapeutic systems.
Adopt holistic frameworks such as the TEQUILA model addressing trust, evidence, and liability.
Establish robust governance mechanisms and interdisciplinary oversight so AI therapy systems are introduced safely and transparently.
Require algorithmic explainability so therapists can understand how and why an AI system reached a conclusion.

screen.reason: This is a theoretical framework and perspective paper proposing a 5-stage taxonomy to govern and conceptualize AI agents and LLMs in psychiatry and psychotherapy.
